title: O Lord! How Happy Should We Be
description: O Lord! How Happy Should We Be in Tonic Solfa to MERIBAH, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 230, “Self-Renunciation”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MERIBAH; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord! how hap-py should we be, If we could leave our cares to Thee, If we from self could rest, And feel at heart that One a-bove, In per-fect wis-dom, per-fect love, Is work-ing for the best.

lines: O Lord! how happy should we be,
If we could leave our cares to Thee,
If we from self could rest,
And feel at heart that One above,
For when we kneel and cast our care
Upon our God in humble prayer,
Sure that our Father, who is nigh
To hear the ravens when they cry,
O, may these trustless hearts of ours
The lesson learn from birds and flowers,
And learn from self to cease, —
Leave all things to our Father's will,
And, on His mercy, leaning still,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MERIBAH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
